claim.markdown_says: ## 15.67.4 Returned value rules   (line 37005 of specs/ISO_COBOL.md — H2), whereas the siblings are '### 15.67.1 General' (36946), '### 15.67.2 General format' (36955) and '### 15.67.3 Argument rules' (36960) — H3
claim.why_it_matters: The heading level makes 15.67.4 a peer of the '## 15.67 NUMVAL function' clause instead of one of its subclauses, so the returned-value rules detach from the NUMVAL function in every TOC/outline/anchor-walk built from the markdown. The same defect recurs for 15.68.4 and 15.69.4, so it is a pattern, not a one-off.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against a fresh 300 dpi render of spec_p924.png (printed folio 894) and specs/ISO_COBOL.md. ATTEMPTED REFUTATIONS, ALL FAILED. (1) 'The text is present, just reflowed' — does not apply: the claim is not that text is missing, and indeed nothing is missing; the heading string, its number, and both numbered rules ('1) The returned value is the numeric value represented by argument-1.' / '2) If argument-1 contains CR, DB, or the minus sign, the returned value is negative.') transcribe verbatim. The defect is the heading LEVEL. (2) 'The claim misquotes a source' — it does not. Verified byte-exactly: line 37005 is '## 15.67.4 Returned value rules' (H2); lines 36946 / 36955 / 36960 are '### 15.67.1 General' / '### 15.67.2 General format' / '### 15.67.3 Argument rules' (H3). All four line numbers in the claim are correct. Line 36943 is '## 15.67 NUMVAL function', so 15.67.4 is emitted at exactly the same level as its own parent clause — a peer, as claimed. (3) 'Page-break furniture' — does not apply: 15.67.4 begins mid-page on 924 with ~two thirds of the page blank below it; no break is involved, and 15.67.1-3 sit on the preceding page 923 where they are correctly H3, so the transcriber changed level across the break for no source reason. (4) 'It is only formatting and does not change meaning' — the strongest candidate, and it is the one that decides severity but not reality. In markdown the heading level is the SOLE encoding of the hierarchy that the PDF encodes through ISO clause numbering; ISO/IEC Directives Part 2 numbering makes a three-part number (15.67.4) a subdivision of the two-part clause (15.67) by definition, so H2 contradicts the source's own structure. It is also self-inconsistent with the transcription's established convention: of 376 headings matching '15.x.y' in the file, 364 are H3 and only 12 are H2, so H3 is unambiguously the intended mapping and these 12 are errors, not a deliberate alternate scheme. No prose is lost and no COBOL semantics change, so this is navigational/structural damage only — correctly filed as 'structural', not semantic.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, with three corrections to the description. (a) The kind label 'missing-heading' is a misnomer — nothing is missing. The heading '15.67.4 Returned value rules' is present at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:37005 with its anchor '' and both of its rules intact. The defect is a heading-LEVEL / nesting error: H2 where the sibling subclauses and the file's own convention use H3, which makes 15.67.4 a peer of '## 15.67 NUMVAL function' (line 36943) rather than its child. Re-file as kind=heading-level. (b) The claim's typographic evidence is wrong even though its conclusion is right. Rendering page 925 shows that in this PDF the clause heading '15.68 NUMVAL-C function' and the subclause headings '15.68.1 General' / '15.68.2 General format' / '15.68.3 Argument rules' are set in the SAME bold serif face at the SAME size, distinguished only by the number depth and the wider tab after the number. So 'printed in the same subclause style as 15.67.1/2/3' cannot by itself establish the level — the printed face is equally consistent with a clause heading. What actually establishes 15.67.4 as a subclause of 15.67 is ISO's clause NUMBERING (a three-part number under a two-part parent), not the typeface. The finding should cite the numbering, not the style, or a reviewer can legitimately knock it down. (c) The pattern is four times wider than stated. It is not just 15.67.4 / 15.68.4 / 15.69.4; twelve '15.x.y' headings are H2 against 364 that are H3 — lines 33440 (15.3.1), 33516 (15.3.2), 33531 (15.3.3), 33664 (15.4.1), 33736 (15.5.3), 33741 (15.5.4), 33746 (15.5.5), 34600 (15.19.3), 34623 (15.19.4), 37005 (15.67.4), 37121 (15.68.4), 37189 (15.69.4). Every one has an H2 parent clause, so all twelve detach identically; 15.5.3-15.5.5 and 15.19.3-15.19.4 are especially clear because their own immediate siblings 15.5.1/15.5.2 and 15.19.1/15.19.2 are correctly H3. Fix all twelve in one pass. Two adjacent observations found while verifying, out of scope for this page but worth logging separately: line 37189 reads '15.69.4 Returned values rules' (plural 'values'), and clause 15's own top level is inconsistent — '## 15 Intrinsic functions' (33331) and '## 15.4 Returned values' (33659) are both H2 while '### 15.3 Arguments' (33366) is H3.
